Wiring (step-skeletons.md steps 1, 5, 6): activate askama 0.12 (already declared in workspace Cargo.toml:38, absent from Cargo.lock) + askama_axum on foundry-app and add askama.toml; re-run cargo deny check (MIT/Apache-2.0). steps.name: Base layout + board template + views.rs view-model; switch show_board to render via template
criteria: Opening the Auth v2 board shows the same columns Backlog, Todo, In-Progress, Done and the same cards (AUTH-2, AUTH-3) in their columns as the current format! board (selector-and-substring-identical)
The board markup links the vendored stylesheet and loads the vendored htmx and Alpine scripts from the application's own /static path
The board references no external origin (no http(s):// or // asset references)
The hidden #kb-items keyboard-navigation carrier is preserved with AUTH-2 before AUTH-3 (ASC), and data-column / data-issue-key markers are byte-stable
An empty board renders the grown, inviting empty state with call-to-action guidance on how to file the first issue
steps.scenario_name: A member opens a styled board that still shows the same issues
steps.implementation_notes: Crafter = @nw-software-crafter (Standard Rust, OOP, EXAMPLE-BASED). Acceptance driver: the us-b01 @walking_skeleton @real-io scenario over the real in-process axum router + real Postgres; unskip this one scenario. Also greens the us-b01 empty-state scenario and the keyboard-carrier scenario as they ride the same render switch (acceptable: one render switch, multiple observable assertions on the same surface). Wiring (step-skeletons.md steps 2, 3, 4): create src/views.rs with #[derive(Template)] structs BaseLayout + BoardPage and the IssueCard partial view-model (the ONE issue-card definition). templates/base.html = the single base layout: <head> with vendored <link rel=stylesheet href=/static/css/foundry.css> + <script src=/static/vendor/htmx.min.js> + alpine, header chrome, {% block content %}. templates/board.html extends base, renders columns and {% include partials/issue_card.html %}, keeps the #kb-items hidden carrier ASC-sorted with data-column/data-issue-key, grows the empty-state copy to invite filing the first issue. Rewire projects::show_board to fetch via foundry_services::board::list_board_issues (UNCHANGED seam), build views::BoardPage, render; DELETE render_board's format!. The OOB-create path in issues.rs renders the SAME issue_card partial. Handlers own data/policy, templates own markup: NO DB call, NO authz, NO sanitization in templates (NFR-WEBB-BND-01). Askama auto-escapes by default. Render contract is selector-and-substring-identical (scraper CSS selectors + visible text + data-* markers), NOT byte-for-byte — the existing us-08 board suite is the regression net and MUST stay green. Unit: std #[test] that views::BoardPage renders expected selectors/markers from a fixed view-model (pure, no I/O). No proptest. Recommend ArchUnit-style enforcement is out of scope; the web!=DB AST guard from Feature A stays green (no sqlx in render path).

steps.name: Render-failure → clean 500 seam (no half-page)
criteria: When the board template is configured to fail rendering, opening the board responds with a clean server error (500), not a 200
The error response is not a partially rendered page (no half-emitted markup)

A test-only AppState flag (parallel to db_unreachable, behind cfg(any(test, feature="test-support"))) drives the board view render to return Err; the handler maps render errors to a clean 500 centrally
The previously-green board scenarios (walking skeleton, empty state, keyboard carrier) stay green
steps.scenario_name: A board template that fails to render returns a clean error, not a half-page
steps.implementation_notes: Crafter = @nw-software-crafter (Standard Rust, OOP, EXAMPLE-BASED). Acceptance driver: the us-b01 @error @real-io render-failure scenario; unskip it. Wiring (step-skeletons.md step 7): add a cfg(any(test, feature="test-support")) AppState flag (mirror the existing db_unreachable flag) that forces the board view render to return Err; the board handler maps any render error to a clean 500 (never a half-page), and an htmx-fragment request maps to a 500 fragment. DELIVER replaces the b_force_template_failure placeholder Given in feature_b_web_tier.rs with the real flag setter (board_template_fails). This is the Earned-Trust render-failure probe: fail-safe, fail-fast, fail-loud. Unit: std #[test] asserting the error-mapping function turns a render Err into a 500 with no body bleed-through. No proptest. Invariant: production render path unchanged; the seam is test-only.

The existing us-06 sign-in scenarios stay green (regression net)

steps.scenario_name: The served htmx asset is a single pinned version 2
steps.implementation_notes: Crafter = @nw-software-crafter (Standard Rust, OOP, EXAMPLE-BASED). Acceptance driver: the us-b05 @walking_skeleton @real-io 'served htmx is v2' scenario; unskip it. The file-issue, post-and-edit-comment, and data-markers-byte-stable scenarios are the DB4 regression net that goes green once the bump lands AND the existing hx-driven scenarios stay green. Wiring (step-skeletons.md steps 13, 14, htmx2-migration.md DD6/DD7): swap the vendored htmx blob to the pinned latest-stable htmx 2.0.x .min.js (replace static/vendor/htmx.min.js, update VENDOR.md provenance + sha256 + the base-layout reference if hashed-named); exactly one htmx file under /static. Normalize the active hx-* directives across base.html and the partials to ONE consistent convention (bare hx-* per the verified reality; centralized after Slices 1-3). Unit: a std #[test] (or xtask check-assets) asserting exactly one vendored htmx file and that its bytes report a 2.x version string. No proptest. Invariant: ONE binary, NO JS toolchain/CDN; data-* markers unchanged; full suite green.
